Last month Dad's room was set up safe after his hospital stay. This month things have moved, and nobody noticed. Second Look tells you what changed in his room — with proof.
Film a twenty-second walkthrough on each visit. It blurs people and papers, finds every object, proves each change, and tells the family.
Here's a sample room. The watchlist is what must stay put — the walker, the lamp, the bag. Type it, or just say it.

Four Meta models work together. SAM 3.1 tracks every object through both videos. Muse Spark takes the inventory and judges what moved. When SAM didn't know the word walker, Spark taught it 'metal walking frame'. Muse Wonder gives a second opinion on borderline calls.
Three things need attention. Every finding shows its evidence — the same lamp, before and after — and ends in plain steps. Ask Dad first.
And Dad has a say. He said he moved the lamp to read by his chair — so it's marked as his choice, not an alarm.

This one is real — a lab I filmed tonight. The chairs were pulled into the aisle, and it caught that. It also thought a trash bin appeared, but the first video never showed that corner, so the claim is struck, with the reason. If we can't show where we saw it, we don't say it.

Family far away get words, never pictures — live. They can ask, 'Where was his walker last seen?' and get an answer with the check it came from. It can even write the update for Dad — to him, not about him.
Next: the same check from his own glasses. He wears the camera, so nobody films him. It whispers where his walker is and remembers where he left things. This is a simulation running the real models.
It will never diagnose Dad, watch him continuously, or claim he took his pills. Four Meta models, about thirty cents a check. Second Look.
